result.instructions:
Web research toolkit: search the web, fetch pages as LLM-friendly markdown with follow-up links, and extract text/tables from documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) and text formats (TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, XML, RSS/Atom). Results are cached, rate-limited per domain, and token-budgeted.

## Rendering (JS pages / anti-bot)

Page fetches use a render strategy: `auto` (static first; stealth browser on failure/non-text), `browser` (stealth first, static fallback), or `static` (never renders). Select it per call with `use_smart` on `web_search` (when not search_only), `inspect_html_page`, `batch_inspect_pages`, and `crawl`, or set the process default with the `GOSSAMER_FETCH_MODE` environment variable. Browser rendering needs the optional `gossamer-web[browser]` extra; `provider='browser'` is the corresponding stealth search engine.

## Skill pack

The `gossamer` agent skill ships inside this package and is readable as the resource `skills://gossamer` (routing, budgets, auth, cache behavior, and the literature-collection recipe). Run `gossamer skills show gossamer` to print it, or `gossamer skills install` to copy it into Claude Code / OpenCode discovery directories.

tools.description:
Unified web search + research. search_only=true (default false) is a pure provider search across engines (duckduckgo/google/bing/exa/browser) returning a deduped list. search_only=false also fetches up to depth candidate pages, returning one record per source with status, markdown, and provenance for a cited synthesis. When fetching, use_smart selects the render strategy.

Args:
    query: The search query / research topic
    search_only: true returns only provider search results; false also fetches up to depth pages and returns per-source records.
    max_results: Maximum number of search results to consider (default: 5).
    depth: Number of candidate pages to fetch when search_only=false (default: 5).
    max_tokens: Global token budget for the whole response (0 = toolbox default).
    provider: Search engine to prefer, in both modes. search_only=false plans the research run through this provider. Falls back through other providers on failure.
    use_smart: Render strategy for fetched pages: 'auto' (default; follows fetch_mode), 'browser' (stealth browser first, static fallback), or 'static' (never renders). Ignored when search_only=true.

tools.name: web_search

tools.description:
Fetch and extract markdown content from a web page. Set use_smart='browser' for JS-rendered pages (SPA, anti-bot); 'auto' (default) follows fetch_mode; 'static' is static-only. If the page exceeds the output budget, pass the research query to keep only the most relevant sections, or offset / max_chunks to page through it in chunks. Returns markdown, follow-up links, and provenance.

Args:
    url: The URL to inspect
    use_smart: Render strategy: 'auto' (default), 'browser' (headless browser first, static on failure), or 'static'.
    query: The research query. When the page exceeds the output budget, only the most relevant sections are returned.
    offset: Character offset into the page markdown to start from; pass the previous call's next_offset to resume.
    max_chunks: Number of consecutive budget-sized chunks to return (each chunk respects the output budget; the total may exceed it).
    structured: true returns a structured payload (metadata, tables, links) instead of raw markdown.

tools.description:
Download a remote file to an explicit local path without requiring document extraction. Streams under the configured/per-call byte cap, follows and revalidates redirects, respects robots.txt and SSRF protections, and validates PDF magic when expected_format='pdf' or the output ends in .pdf. Existing destinations are preserved unless overwrite=true. Optional fallback_urls are caller-supplied OA/repository candidates tried sequentially; every URL is checked independently and bot walls are never bypassed.

Args:
    source: Remote HTTP(S) URL to download
    output_path: Local destination file path
    min_bytes: Minimum accepted file size in bytes (default: 1).
    max_bytes: Maximum bytes (0 uses the configured max_response_bytes cap).
    expected_format: 'auto' validates PDF when output_path ends in .pdf; 'pdf' always validates the %PDF- signature.
    overwrite: Replace an existing destination only when true.
    resume: Continue an existing partial file with Range/If-Range; servers that ignore Range restart the file.
    fallback_urls: Optional caller-supplied ordered OA/repository mirrors to try sequentially after the primary URL; every candidate still obeys robots/SSRF checks.

expected_format.title: Expected Format

fallback_urls.title: Fallback Urls

max_bytes.title: Max Bytes

tools.name: locate_pdf

tools.description:
Extract text content from documents via URL or local path: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, plus text formats (TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, XML) and RSS/Atom feeds. For large documents, pass pages (e.g. '10-20') to read a page range instead of the whole file.

Args:
    source: URL or local file path to the document
    pages: 1-based inclusive page range for PDFs ('10', '10-20', '10-', '-20'); for XLSX the range selects sheets. Omitted -> the whole document.
    structured: true returns a validated ParsedDocumentPayload (metadata, pages, tables) as JSON instead of plain text.
    store: true writes the original bytes and the full extracted text to disk under store_dir; the result includes a 'stored' object with paths and sizes. Cannot combine with pages=.
    store_dir: Directory to write stored files into (created if missing). Only used when store=true.
    include_images: PDF only; requires store=true. Also extract embedded raster images into <stem>.files/ with a ## Figures section (reported under stored.resources). Vector-only figures are skipped; tables render by default.
    tables_as: Rendering of spreadsheet (XLSX) tables in the returned content: 'json' (default; array of {sheet, headers, rows}), 'markdown' (pipe tables), or 'csv' (comma-separated, one ## <sheet> block per sheet). Other formats keep markdown rendering.
    prefer_jats: JATS-first scholarly route (default true): DOI-resolvable sources try publisher full-text XML (EuropePMC, then PLOS) via the in-house _core JATS kernel before the PDF path. pages= with a JATS-resolvable source errors; structured=true or tables_as != 'markdown' skips the route.

tools.name: extract_document

tools.description:
Discover a site's structured resources without crawling the link graph (Tier 3.12). Finds feed declarations (<link rel=alternate> RSS/Atom/Feed-JSON) on the page and probes the site root for /sitemap.xml, following bounded sitemap indexes. Returns deduplicated, budgeted lists of feed URLs and sitemap page URLs.

Args:
    url: A page or site URL to discover resources for

url.description: A page or site URL to discover resources for
url.title: Url

tools.name: discover_resources

tools.description:
Relevance-ranked crawl of a URL's link graph (cross-domain by default) to find the pages most relevant to a query. Walks from root_url, scoring candidates by query relevance that decays with depth, so the page budget lands on the most relevant links. Optionally seed with a site-scoped search (search_prior) and/or extra URLs (seed_urls). Returns per page: title, relevance score, and a short skim; plus unfetched document links and skipped links. Full pages stay cached for later re-reads.

Args:
    root_url: Seed URL to start the traversal from
    query: Relevance focus for the frontier ranking. When omitted, the root page's own title and content words stand in for it.
    max_depth: Maximum link hops from the root (0 = root only; hard cap 5)
    max_pages: Total pages fetched across all depths (1-50); failed fetches do not count
    same_host: When true, follow only links on the root's host (www. ignored); false follows external links too
    min_score: Minimum relevance score for a candidate to enter the frontier (0 = follow everything that passes the boilerplate filters)
    excerpts: Also return a keyword-densest 300-char excerpt per page (raises the payload size; pair with a lower max_pages)
    search_prior: Before traversing, run one site-scoped web search and feed its top results into the frontier at depth 1 (exempt from min_score; a failed search is non-fatal)
    seed_urls: Extra starting URLs, pushed at depth 0 (children at depth 1); they respect min_score
    use_smart: Render strategy for crawled pages: 'auto' (default), 'browser' (headless first), or 'static'.

tools.name: crawl

tools.description:
Unified cache maintenance. action='clear' wipes the memory and disk caches plus the visited-URL set (force fresh fetches); action='prune' (default) removes expired entries and evicts to the size cap while keeping valid ones; action='reset' forgets visited URLs without clearing caches (retry a failed page).

Args:
    action: Cache operation: 'clear' (wipe caches + visited), 'prune' (default, evict expired/LRU to size cap), or 'reset' (forget visited URLs only).

action.description: Cache operation: 'clear' (wipe caches + visited), 'prune' (default, evict expired/LRU to size cap), or 'reset' (forget visited URLs only).
action.title: Action

tools.name: manage_cache

tools.description:
Category-aware, provider-specific search. Classifies the query into a domain category (scholarly, legal, patent, financial, geo, general) and calls that category's default provider. Omit the query to return the full taxonomy (category descriptions and provider ids) as JSON. Pass provider=<id> to call a specific source; pass category=<name> to skip classification. No automatic fallback between providers -- the caller chooses. Pass providers=[...] for an explicit scholarly multi-search merged by DOI/arXiv ID. OpenAlex-only filter/select/title/author options pass through to that API. Returns the chosen category, provider, and results as JSON. Provider failures keep results as an empty list and add a top-level error field.

Args:
    query: The search query. Omit it to return the full category -> provider taxonomy as JSON instead, so you can discover which provider to use.
    category: Optional category to use directly (e.g. 'scholarly', 'legal', 'financial', 'geo', 'general'); skips classification. Pair with provider= to pick a source within it.
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    provider: Optional provider id to call (see the taxonomy from a no-query call). Given alone, its owning category is used; with category= it must belong to that category. Omitted -> the category's default provider. No automatic fallback.
    filter: OpenAlex-native filter expression; valid only with provider='openalex'.
    select: OpenAlex-native comma-separated field projection; valid only with provider='openalex'.
    title: OpenAlex title search; maps to verified title.search filter. Valid only with provider='openalex'.
    author: OpenAlex author search; maps to verified raw_author_name.search filter. Valid only with provider='openalex'.
    providers: Explicit providers for sequential scholarly search/merge, e.g. ['openalex', 'arxiv']. Mutually exclusive with provider= and supported only for scholarly.

    dedupe: Collapse records that share a DOI or URL before formatting.
    from_pdf: Treat every string input as a local PDF path and cite its detected DOI; PDFs without a DOI return an error.

tools.description:
Probe whether source URLs are reachable without downloading their pages (Workstream 2). Takes a list of URLs (strings or {url} dicts), validates each through the SSRF guard, runs a lightweight status probe per URL (polite / parallel / bounded), and returns per-URL status: ok (2xx/3xx), unreachable (4xx/5xx), blocked (SSRF), or error (network/timeout). Reuses the shared fetch pipeline -- no new HTTP surface.

Args:
    urls: List of URLs to probe (plain strings or {url} dicts).
    mode: Probe mode: 'status' (HEAD/minimal GET, default) or 'content' (full fetch).

contents.text:
---
name: gossamer
description: Web research toolkit (search, fetch pages as markdown, extract documents, patent/legal/financial domain research). Use whenever the task needs current external information â€” docs, APIs, papers, case law, market data, patents â€” instead of guessing from training data. Prefers cached, rate-limited, token-budgeted tools over raw curl/fetch loops.
---

# Gossamer

Web research toolkit: search the web, fetch pages as LLM-friendly markdown
with follow-up links, and extract text/tables from documents (PDF, DOCX,
XLSX, PPTX, feeds). Domain adapters route scholarly / legal / patent /
financial / geo queries to the right APIs. Everything is cached,
per-domain rate-limited, and token-budgeted.

## Access (use whichever the harness provides)

- **MCP tools** (`gossamer_*` in pi with directTools, or plain names in
  Codex/Claude Code): `web_search`, `inspect_html_page`,
  `batch_inspect_pages`, `download_file`, `locate_pdf`, `extract_document`,
  `discover_resources`, `crawl`, `manage_cache`, `research_by_category`,
  `export_citations`, `check_sources`.
- **MCP resource** `skills://gossamer`: this file, readable from any MCP
  host without a repo checkout.
- **CLI** (identical JSON, no MCP setup; 14 subcommands â€” the 12 MCP tools
  1:1, plus `categories` and `skills`): `search QUERY [--max-results N --max-tokens T
  --search-only --provider P --depth D --use-smart auto|browser|static]` Â· `research QUERY [--category C
  --provider P --providers Pâ€¦ --max-results N --filter F --select F --title T --author A]` Â· `inspect URL [--query Q --offset N
  --max-chunks N --structured --use-smart auto|browser|static]` Â·
  `batch URLâ€¦ [--use-smart auto|browser|static]` Â· `download URL -o PATH [--min-bytes N --max-bytes N --expect-format auto|pdf --overwrite --resume --try-mirrors URLâ€¦]` Â·
  `locate-pdf DOI` Â· `extract FILE|URL [--pages A-B --structured --tables-as json|markdown|csv --store
  --store-dir D --include-images]` Â· `check URLâ€¦ [--mode status|content]` Â·
  `discover URL` Â· `crawl ROOT [--query Q --max-depth D --max-pages N
  --min-score S --same-host --excerpts --search-prior --seed-urls Uâ€¦
  --use-smart auto|browser|static]` Â· `cache [--action prune|clear|reset]` Â·
  `cite DOI|URL|PDFâ€¦ [--style bibtex|csl-json|apa|mla --enrich --no-dedupe --from-pdf]` Â·
  `categories` Â·
  `skills list|show|install [--dest DIRâ€¦] [--project] [--skill NAMEâ€¦] [--force]`.
  Run via the project venv
  (`â€¦/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m gossamer.cli â€¦` on Windows); `skills
  show gossamer` prints this file, and `skills install` copies it into
  Claude Code / OpenCode skill directories. CLI defaults:
  `--max-results 5` (search/research), `--depth 5`, `--max-tokens 0`
  (budget default), crawl `--max-depth 3 --max-pages 15 --min-score 0.05`.
  `--fetch-mode auto|browser|static` sets the render baseline for the whole
  run; `--use-smart` overrides it per page-fetching command.

## Tool call signatures (defaults shown; one JSON envelope per call)

Required parameters have no default. `None`/empty means "not supplied";
`0` budgets mean "toolbox default".

### Search & read

```python
web_search(query, search_only=False, max_results=5, depth=5,
           max_tokens=0, provider="duckduckgo", use_smart="auto")
inspect_html_page(url, use_smart="auto", query=None, offset=0,
                  max_chunks=1, structured=False)
batch_inspect_pages(urls, use_smart="auto")
crawl(root_url, query=None, max_depth=3, max_pages=15, same_host=False,
      min_score=0.05, excerpts=False, search_prior=False, seed_urls=[],
      use_smart="auto")
```

`crawl` caps: `max_depth` hard cap 5, `max_pages` 1-50 (failed fetches do
not count). `use_smart` applies to every page-fetching tool (`web_search`
when it fetches, `inspect_html_page`, `batch_inspect_pages`, `crawl`);
`use_smart="browser"` needs the `gossamer-web[browser]` extra. Browser
batches are sequential; `auto` is static-first with a stealth fallback.

### Documents & files

```python
extract_document(source, pages=None, structured=False, store=False,
                 store_dir=None, include_images=False, tables_as="json",
                 prefer_jats=True)
download_file(source, output_path, min_bytes=1, max_bytes=0,
              expected_format="auto", overwrite=False, resume=False,
              fallback_urls=[])
discover_resources(url)
check_sources(urls, mode="status")
```

`extract_document(pages="10-20")` is 1-based inclusive for PDFs (sheet
range for XLSX) and cannot combine with `store=True`; `include_images`
needs `store=True` and is PDF-only. Scholarly extraction prefers publisher
full text (JATS XML via EuropePMC, then PLOS) when resolvable
(`prefer_jats=True`, default); `pages=` with a JATS-resolvable source
errors, `structured=True` or `tables_as!="markdown"` skips the route,
and `include_images` is a no-op on the JATS route (remote hrefs, not saved). `download_file(max_bytes=0)` uses the
configured cap; `fallback_urls` are caller-supplied mirrors, each checked
independently. `check_sources(mode="status")` is a HEAD probe;
`"content"` is a GET for hosts that reject HEAD.

### Research & citations

```python
research_by_category(query=None, category=None, max_results=5,
                     provider=None, filter=None, select=None, title=None,
                     author=None, providers=[])
locate_pdf(doi)
export_citations(results, style="bibtex", enrich=False, dedupe=True,
                 from_pdf=False)
manage_cache(action="prune")
```

`research_by_category(query)` with no category auto-routes; omit `query`
entirely to get the provider taxonomy. `filter`/`select`/`title`/`author`
are valid only with `provider="openalex"` and rejected otherwise;
`providers=[...]` is scholarly-only and mutually exclusive with
`provider`. `locate_pdf` locates candidates, it never downloads.

## Routing (don't guess â€” classify first)

`research` auto-routes, or pick explicitly. Category â†’ default provider:

- `scholarly` â†’ `openalex` by default; `crossref`, `arxiv`, `zenodo`, `semanticscholar`, `huggingface` (models + cards), and `huggingface-papers` (Daily Papers, arXiv-joined, search-only) are opt-in scholarly providers. Hub search is conjunctive â€” prefer short queries (`stable diffusion model`, not full sentences)
- `legal` â†’ `courtlistener` (US case law) Â· `oldp` (German cases) Â·
  `hudoc` (ECtHR) Â· `ecfr`/`federalregister`/`govinfo` (US regs)
- `patent` â†’ `epo` (worldwide via INPADOC) Â· `kipris` (Korea) Â·
  `patentsview` (USPTO) Â· `lens` (WO/EP/DE/CN/US aggregator) â€” key-gated, fail fast without keys Â·
  `google-patents` (keyless number lookup; free text via `site:patents.google.com` search)

`research --filter F --select F --title T --author A` passes OpenAlex-native controls and is valid
only with `--provider openalex`; gossamer rejects these options for other

`title.search`/`raw_author_name.search` filters and combine with `--filter`. `--providers` explicitly runs a
sequential scholarly merge by DOI/arXiv ID; it never runs by default and keeps
all per-provider source records.

Provider failures from `research` keep `results` as an empty list and put the
message in a top-level `error` field. The CLI exits nonzero for these failures.
For arXiv HTTP 406, which can reflect a temporary upstream edge/IP limit,
avoid immediate repeat calls and honor the provider's three-second minimum.

## Budgets (avoid harness timeouts)

- `use_smart="browser"` (JS rendering) needs the `gossamer-web[browser]`
  extra, Windows/macOS only â€” without it browser-first falls back to
  static and browser-only modes raise a clear dependency error. Even with
  it, bot-walled sites (Cloudflare challenges, CAPTCHAs) still fail.
  Explicit `browser`/`static` requests bypass a cached result produced by
  the other engine; the reply's `fetch_method` reports `static`, `browser`,
  or `stealth-fallback`. Browser batches are sequential, so keep them small.
  Renders run in a child process (45s timeout): a native engine abort/hang
  becomes a fetch error: browser-first falls back to static, strict browser
  failures return an error, and the host stays alive.
  `GOSSAMER_BROWSER_ISOLATION=0` is debug-only.
- Keep `max_pages` â‰¤ 15 on crawls; set an explicit `max_tokens` budget.
- Long extractions: `extract â€¦ --pages 10-20` instead of whole documents.
- `check` URLs with `--mode status` before fetching the shaky ones.

## Auth

API keys live in the keystore (`~/.gossamer/keys.json`;
`python -m gossamer.keystore --init`), never in harness configs or prompts.
Keyed providers raise an actionable error naming the exact variable
(e.g. `GOSSAMER_EPO_KEY`) â€” surface it to the user instead of retrying.
OpenAlex works keyless for casual use; `GOSSAMER_OPENALEX_KEY` is optional
and raises the API's daily budget. Set `GOSSAMER_OPENALEX_EMAIL` to send your
own `mailto` contact; gossamer does not invent a default email. OpenAlex
429s come in two documented kinds: a per-second rate limit (wait a moment
and retry) and a daily credit-budget refusal (`not_enough_credits` â€” wait
for the daily reset; the typed error carries `X-RateLimit-Reset` seconds).
Semantic Scholar can run keyless, but its unauthenticated pool is shared and
may return 429. Configure `GOSSAMER_SEMANTICSCHOLAR_API_KEY` for the
individual one-request-per-second allowance; if keyless use returns 429,
wait or set that exact variable rather than looping retries.

## Config / cache (where stuff actually is)

- Cache: `GOSSAMER_CACHE_DIR` (see `mcp.json`) > `gossamer.json:cache_dir` > `./.gossamer_cache`.
- Render baseline: `GOSSAMER_FETCH_MODE` > `gossamer.json:fetch_mode` > `auto`; CLI `--fetch-mode` overrides it for one run, and `--use-smart`/`use_smart` overrides it per call.
- Keys: `$GOSSAMER_KEYSTORE` > `gossamer.json:keystore` > `~/.gossamer/keys.json` (created only via `keystore --init`; absent = normal, not a broken install).
- Check effective paths in `mcp.json` + `python -m gossamer.keystore --check`, not `~/.gossamer`.

## Cache behavior (when a result is cached)

- Page/document reads are cached: `inspect`/`extract` responses carry `cache_hit: true` when served from cache; repeat reads within the TTL skip the network. Paging (`--offset`/`--max-chunks`, `--pages`) reads the cached full text, so re-reads stay cheap.
- `search` results are cached per query for the configured TTL; repeats do not re-query the provider. Provider adapters (`research --provider â€¦`) are live calls with per-domain rate limits, not result caches.
- `check`, `download`, `locate-pdf`, and `cite` are never cached: `check` probes liveness, `download` writes files, `locate-pdf` resolves current OA state, and `cite` formats on demand.
- Maintenance: `cache --action prune` drops expired/over-cap entries (keeps valid ones and visited URLs); `clear` wipes caches plus visited URLs for fully fresh fetches; `reset` forgets visited URLs only, to retry a failed page without clearing caches.
- No global PATH shim is provided: run the CLI from the project venv (`â€¦/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m gossamer.cli â€¦` on Windows) or via MCP tools.

## Documents (PDF limits that matter)

- Tables render as markdown tables by default â€” no flag needed.
- Figures need `extract â€¦ --store --include-images` (PDF only): rasters land in `<stem>.files/` with a `## Figures` section; without the flag (or without `--store`) you get text-only and an empty manifest. Vector-only figures have no bytes to save.
- Large PDFs: use `--pages 10-20` ranges (cannot combine with `--store`).
- Use `download URL -o file.pdf --expect-format pdf` to save a remote file without parsing it; use `extract URL --store` when you also want extracted text. Downloads obey robots/SSRF checks, enforce a byte cap, and never bypass bot walls. Add `--resume` to continue an existing partial file with Range/If-Range (servers that ignore Range restart; unsatisfiable ranges keep the partial file). `--try-mirrors` accepts only caller-supplied, known OA/repository URLs; each is checked independently and attempts are returned with provenance.

## Literature collection workflow

1. Search via `research QUERY --category scholarly --max-results N`; use `--providers openalex arxiv` only when you explicitly want a sequential multi-provider merge.
2. Probe candidate pages with `check URL --mode status` before spending a full fetch/download.
3. For a DOI, run `locate-pdf DOI`, inspect the returned `candidates`, and prefer an OA PDF URL with clear source/license metadata. This step locates candidates; it does not fetch the file. OpenAlex runs first; Unpaywall v2 is queried only when `GOSSAMER_UNPAYWALL_EMAIL` is configured and OpenAlex yields nothing usable.
4. Download with `download URL -o paper.pdf --expect-format pdf`. If a known OA repository mirror is already available, pass it with `--try-mirrors URLâ€¦`; each URL is still checked independently and no challenge is bypassed.
5. Parse the saved file with `extract paper.pdf`; add `--store --store-dir DIR` if you also want the extracted Markdown/resources persisted.
6. Export a citation with `cite DOI --style bibtex` (or another supported style), or `cite paper.pdf [--from-pdf]` to cite a downloaded PDF via its detected DOI. Review license/access terms before redistributing any full text.
